SNAP Benefit Loss Affects Families 
 NEWS Community News 
 Senator Marilyn Stricklyn Visits Make a Difference Foundation to Discuss SNAP Benefit Loss
 By John Weymer • 
 Wed, Oct 28, 2026 
 Senator Marilyn Stricklyn Visits Make a Difference Foundation to Discuss SNAP Benefit Loss 
 Senator Marilyn Stricklyn recently visited the Make a Difference Foundation to discuss how the loss or reduction of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits is affecting families and individuals in the community.
 During the visit, Stricklyn met with foundation representatives and community members to hear about the challenges faced by households struggling to afford groceries. Discussions focused on food insecurity, the rising cost of essentials and the increased pressure placed on food banks, meal programs and other local assistance organizations when residents lose access to SNAP benefits.
 The Make a Difference Foundation emphasized the importance of ensuring that vulnerable residents have access to reliable food resources. For many families, SNAP benefits help cover the cost of groceries throughout the month, particularly for seniors, children, people with disabilities and households facing unemployment or rising living expenses.
 Stricklyn’s visit also provided an opportunity to discuss potential community and legislative responses, including strengthening local food assistance programs and connecting residents with available resources. Foundation leaders said continued collaboration among elected officials, nonprofit organizations and residents will be essential as the community responds to the loss of benefits.
 “The rising cost of groceries is hurting families in the South Sound and across the nation, but help is on the way,” said Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland (WA-10). “At the start of the new Congress in January, I am committed to restoring food assistance, Medicaid cuts, and lowering the cost of living."
 “Visits like this help bring attention to the real challenges families are facing,” foundation representatives said. “We appreciate the opportunity to share what we are seeing and to work toward solutions that help ensure no one in our community goes hungry.”
 The Make a Difference Foundation continues to provide support and connect residents with food, social-service and emergency-assistance resources. Community members seeking help are encouraged to contact the foundation directly or visit local food banks and community assistance programs.
